name: Fire assay laboratory (one furnace batch of production samples)
summary: The company's own assay office fire-assays the mine's underground chip, muck and test-hole samples, the mill's shift composites and the doré bar samples so that geologists can mark ore and waste and the metallurgist can balance the mill. For this mine the laboratory sits in the town of Wawa, about an hour and a half by road from the mine, so sealed samples travel on a daily company shuttle. Technicians log, dry, crush, split and pulverise each sample, fuse a 30 g charge with litharge flux, cupel and part the bead and weigh the gold, in furnace batches of 28 positions that include a blank, a duplicate and a reference standard. Turnaround is set by the shuttle, the drying and furnace queues and re-assays of high-grade samples with visible gold, and the lab is not accredited, so it inserts less quality control than a commercial laboratory.

baseline.org_archetype: A 300-person single-mine Ontario gold producer that runs a non-accredited company fire assay office in the nearest town for production samples and sends exploration core to commercial laboratories.
baseline.notes: Modelled on a single-mine northern Ontario gold producer (Eagle River mine and mill near Wawa) as described in the organisation file; site practice from the Eagle River technical reports where they say it.

unit_of_work: one furnace batch of 28 positions (about 25 production samples plus a reagent blank, a duplicate and a reference standard)
trigger: A geology technician or mill operator seals a set of sample bags with a submission sheet for the daily shuttle.
end_state: Gold results for the batch pass the laboratory's quality checks and are loaded into the geology database or the mill workbook; pulps and rejects are stored and a share of pulps is sent to an outside laboratory as a check.

volume.seasonality: Steady; slightly higher when development is in high-grade zones with heavy face sampling, and at month end when mill inventory and bar samples are added.

evidence.note: Furnace batches hold 28 samples including a reagent blank, a duplicate and a reference standard (srk2022). The organisation file's 5,000-11,000 production samples a month divided by about 25 client samples per batch gives 200-440 batches; the organisation file's 160 batches assumed about 50 samples per batch.

surge.cause: Definition drilling campaign whose core is assayed at the mine lab when commercial labs are backlogged

evidence.note: A small portion of definition core is assayed at the Wesdome laboratory (island2020, srk2022); frequency and size of campaigns are the author's estimate.

Organisation file role (6 people). All six organisation-file technicians are counted as working on production batches. The lab is in Wawa and run as day and evening shifts by local staff rather than a 14/14 camp rotation, so extended_hours is used. Hands-on time per batch implies about eleven technicians for this volume alone, and the lab also assays the neighbouring Island Gold mine's production samples (island2020), so the real crew was larger. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

roles.title: Assay lab superintendent or shift supervisor

evidence.note: Organisation file role (1 people). Matches the 'shift supervisors / Assay Lab Superintendent' who review QC data (srk2022); the organisation file has one supervisor. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

Organisation file role (6 people). Seals and lists underground samples for the shuttle; most samples are collected in the grade control process. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.
Organisation file role (5 people). Imports and checks results in the geology database. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.
Organisation file role (1 people). Reviews outside check assays and lab QC each month. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

roles.title: Site services driver (daily Wawa sample shuttle)

evidence.note: A company shuttle carries samples to the Wawa laboratory daily (srk2022). The organisation file has no driver role; cost assumes a 24-29 CAD/h light-truck driver wage times 1.35. FTE is one round trip of about 3.5 hours a day shared with other site errands.

systems.name: Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network

resources.name: Company assay office in Wawa (preparation, fire assay, AA; not accredited)
Sample preparation line (drying ovens, jaw crusher, riffle splitters, ring pulverisers)

steps.name: Seal and list samples for the shuttle
steps.description: At the end of shift the geology technician collects the tied sample bags from the sample boxes beside the geology office, checks each tag against the sampling sheets, writes the submission list with sample numbers and sample types and seals the bags into shipping bins.

error.defect_description: Sample number missing from the list or tag unreadable.

next.condition: road closed by snow or washout

evidence.note: Bags tied with wire and deposited in sample boxes between the geology office and warehouse (srk2022); bags sealed and shipped daily (island2020). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Drive samples to the Wawa assay office
steps.description: The driver loads the bins, drives the gravel access road and the highway to the assay office in Wawa with the day's mine and mill samples, unloads them at the receiving bench and brings back returns. Touch time is this batch's share of a 3 to 4 hour round trip that carries about ten batches.

error.defect_description: A bin left behind at the mine.

control.basis: Sample security: sealed bags and bins, chain-of-custody list signed at receipt

evidence.note: Company shuttle to the laboratory in Wawa daily (srk2022); access is 70 km of gravel road plus 50 km of highway, about 1.5 hours (wdo2016).

steps.name: Receive and log batch in LIMS
steps.description: A technician places the bags in numerical order by sample type, checks them against the submission list, prepares a list when none came, and enters the batch in the laboratory information system, which assigns furnace positions for the blank, duplicate and standard.

error.defect_description: Batch logged under the wrong sample type or client.

evidence.note: Samples placed in numerical order by product type and verified against the client packing list; a list is prepared and emailed when absent (srk2022, appendix C). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Hold samples while the road is closed
steps.description: When snow, freezing rain or a washout closes the access road, the samples stay locked in the bins at the mine until the shuttle can run, and the geologists mark headings on visual estimates.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Winter storms on the 70 km gravel access road (wdo2016 gives the road); closure frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve submission discrepancy
steps.description: The assay supervisor emails or phones the geology office or mill about the missing or extra bags, corrects the list in LIMS and notes the discrepancy on the receipt letter.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Labs send a letter on receipt detailing the shipment received (island2020). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Dry samples
steps.description: A technician transfers wet chip, muck and test-hole samples to drying pans, loads them into the drying oven and keeps the tags with each pan in assay order. Drying itself takes several hours and is counted as the wait before crushing.

error.defect_description: Tag separated from its pan.

evidence.note: Samples are dried if necessary and maintained in assay order with tags (srk2022). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Crush and riffle split
steps.description: The technician crushes each dried sample in the jaw crusher to about a quarter inch, blows the crusher clean with compressed air between samples, runs barren rock after high-grade samples, and riffle-splits about 300 g for pulverising, bagging the reject for storage.

error.defect_description: Cross-contamination from a high-grade sample.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 and laboratory procedure: hearing protection, dust extraction and guarding on crushers

evidence.note: Jaw crusher to 1/4 inch, cleaned with 120 psi air between samples, Jones riffle split to about 300 g, excess bagged for the client (srk2022). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Pulverise and screen-test
steps.description: The technician pulverises each split in ring pulverisers to minus 150 mesh, cleans the bowls with air and runs silica sand between batches, and screen-tests the first sample of the batch, recording the result in the logbook.

error.defect_description: Pulp not fine enough after a worn bowl.

evidence.note: Bico Braun pulverisers, silica sand between batches, first sample screen-tested (srk2022); an unsuitable pulveriser was replaced after a 2019 external audit (island2020). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Weigh charges and add flux
steps.description: The fire assayer weighs a 30 g aliquot of each pulp into a crucible with premixed litharge flux, adds nitre or flour as the sample needs and a silver inquart, and places the reagent blank, duplicate and Rocklabs reference material in their positions.

error.defect_description: Charge weighed into the wrong crucible position.

control.basis: Ontario O. Reg. 490/09 (designated substances, lead) and laboratory fume extraction procedure for litharge fluxes and lead buttons

evidence.note: Premixed litharge, sodium carbonate, borax, silica and fluorspar flux with nitre or flour and silver collector; each batch of 28 includes a blank, a duplicate and Rocklabs reference material (srk2022); 30 g charge (island2020). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Fuse, pour and recover lead buttons
steps.description: The fire assayer loads the crucibles into the fusion furnace at about 1,950 F for an hour, pours the melts into conical moulds, lets them cool, breaks off the slag and hammers each lead button clean.

error.defect_description: Button too small or too large, or a crucible spills.

control.basis: Ontario O. Reg. 490/09 (designated substances, lead) and laboratory fume extraction procedure for litharge fluxes and lead buttons

evidence.note: Fusion at 1,950 F for 60 minutes, poured into conical moulds, slag removed (srk2022); fusion repeated when the button is too small or large (macassa2019). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Cupel, part and weigh gold beads
steps.description: The fire assayer cupels the buttons, flattens each dore bead, parts the silver in hot dilute nitric acid, washes, anneals and weighs the gold on the microbalance, and the weights are entered against each sample number in LIMS.

error.defect_description: Bead lost or weighed in the wrong order.

control.basis: Ontario O. Reg. 490/09 (designated substances, lead) and laboratory fume extraction procedure for litharge fluxes and lead buttons

evidence.note: Cupellation, parting in nitric acid and weighing on a Mettler XP2U microbalance; gravimetric finish (srk2022, appendix C). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review batch quality control
steps.description: The shift supervisor checks the blank, duplicate and reference standard against their limits, looks at the high-grade results and any sample that does not fit its neighbours, and decides whether to release the batch, re-assay selected pulps or re-fuse the whole batch.

error.defect_description: A biased standard accepted.

control.basis: Laboratory QA/QC procedure (lab not accredited): blank, duplicate and reference material in every furnace batch, supervisor review

next.condition: standard or blank fails, batch re-fused

evidence.note: QA/QC data reviewed by shift supervisors and the Assay Lab Superintendent, with extra checks on anomalous values (srk2022); lab is not certified and its QC is less rigorous than commercial labs (island2020, wdo2016). Shares: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Re-assay selected pulps
steps.description: A technician re-weighs and re-fires the high-grade or out-of-pattern pulps, or prepares a second split from the reject where the gold is coarse, and adds the repeat results beside the originals for the supervisor.

error.defect_description: Repeat entered over the original instead of beside it.

control.basis: Ontario O. Reg. 490/09 (designated substances, lead) and laboratory fume extraction procedure for litharge fluxes and lead buttons

evidence.note: Visible gold is common at Eagle River (wdo2016). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Release results by email
steps.description: The assay supervisor releases the batch in LIMS and emails the results file or certificate to the mine geology office or the mill metallurgist, flagging repeats and any sample still pending.

error.defect_description: File sent to the wrong distribution list.

evidence.note: Results reported by email to the mine sites (wdo2016). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Import and check results in the geology database
steps.description: The mine geologist imports the results into the geology database, checks that sample numbers match the face maps and muck tickets, compares grades with the mapped geology, and uses them to confirm or change the ore and waste marks for the next round. Mill results go to the metallurgist's workbook instead.

error.defect_description: Result attached to the wrong face.

next.condition: suspected sample swap or impossible grade

evidence.note: Production assay QC is reported to the mine geology department, which relies on the lab's internal QC (srk2022). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Query suspected swap with the lab
steps.description: The geologist emails the assay supervisor with the suspect sample numbers and the reason, and the lab checks its logbook and furnace sheet and re-assays the pulps or rejects.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Store pulps and rejects
steps.description: A technician boxes the pulps and coarse rejects in sample-number order, labels the box with the batch number and shelves it in the pulp store, and once a month pulls about one batch in twenty for outside check assays.

error.defect_description: Box shelved out of order.

evidence.note: Pulps are sent to Actlabs as checks on production assays (island2020). Shares and times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Ship check pulps to a commercial laboratory
steps.description: The assay supervisor selects about 5 percent of mineralised pulps from the month's batches, re-numbers them blind, adds certified standards and ships them by courier to an accredited commercial laboratory with a submission form.

error.defect_description: Blind numbering key lost.

control.basis: QA/QC program: periodic check assays of mine-lab pulps at an accredited laboratory

evidence.note: About 5% of mineralised samples re-tested at a second commercial lab (macassa2019); pulps sent to Actlabs (island2020). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for commercial lab results
steps.description: The accredited commercial laboratory receives the courier box, logs the blind-numbered check pulps, fire-assays them in its own queue and emails a signed certificate to the assay supervisor.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Commercial lab turnaround of two to four weeks for check pulps: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Compare check assays and report bias
steps.description: The assay supervisor pairs the check results with the originals, plots them and calculates the share of pairs within tolerance and any bias, and sends the summary to the chief geologist.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Check-assay comparison reported as percent of pairs within 25 percent of each other (macassa2019). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review lab QC and check assays
steps.description: The chief geologist reviews the check-assay summary and the month's standard and blank charts, discusses turnaround and any drift with the assay supervisor, and records actions such as a pulveriser repair or a re-assay campaign.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: NI 43-101 data verification: qualified person reviews assay quality supporting reserves and grade control

evidence.note: Chief mine geologist made quarterly lab visits to assess internal QC and discuss turnaround (macassa2019). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in mine-site fire assay laboratories, 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Re-assay of high-grade or odd samples
exceptions.description: Coarse visible gold gives erratic results, so the supervisor has selected pulps re-fired before release.

exceptions.name: Batch re-fused after QC failure
exceptions.description: The reference standard or blank falls outside limits, and the whole furnace batch is re-weighed and re-fused.

exceptions.name: Access road closed
exceptions.description: Snow or a washout on the gravel access road stops the shuttle, and samples wait at the mine.

exceptions.name: Outside check assays
exceptions.description: About one batch in twenty has pulps sent blind to an accredited laboratory and compared.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from samples sealed at the mine to results in the geology database
benchmarks.population: Company fire assay office serving an Ontario underground gold mine with a daily shuttle

evidence.note: Daily shuttle and emailed results (wdo2016, srk2022) imply next-day results for most batches; spread from re-assays and furnace queues is the author's estimate.

benchmarks.unit: crucible positions including one reagent blank, one duplicate and one reference material

evidence.note: Appendix C of the 2022 technical report.

benchmarks.unit: percent of samples that are QC samples (reliance on duplicates)

evidence.note: Table 11-2 of the Island Gold report gives 5 to 10% internal QC for the Wesdome lab.

pain_points.description: Samples ride 1.5 hours to Wawa once a day, so a round sampled after the shuttle leaves waits a day before it is even crushed and headings are marked without assays.

evidence.note: Daily company shuttle to Wawa (srk2022); trip about 1.5 hours (wdo2016).

pain_points.description: Coarse visible gold makes repeats common and slows release of high-grade batches.

evidence.note: Visible gold at Eagle River is common (wdo2016).

pain_points.description: The lab is not accredited and inserts no QC with muck and test-hole samples, so bias is caught late by outside checks.

evidence.note: Mine assay office is not a certified laboratory (srk2022); Wesdome does not include QC materials with muck and test-hole samples (island2020).

pain_points.description: One preparation line and one fusion furnace set the pace; a worn pulveriser or furnace repair backs up every client.

evidence.note: A 2019 external audit led to replacing an unsuitable pulveriser (island2020).

sources.supports: Comparable mine lab assays mill, bullion and mine samples; QA/QC tracked daily on a spreadsheet; fusion repeated for small or large buttons; LIMS introduced 2018; tight turnaround requirements; chief mine geologist's quarterly lab visits; about 5% of mineralised samples re-tested at a second lab; check-assay pairs within 25%.

assumptions: Simulated median cycle time is about 1.8 days against a tier C estimate of 1.5 days; most of the elapsed time is the wait for the once-a-day shuttle and drying, not furnace work.

The laboratory is the company's assay office in the town of Wawa, not a room at the mill as the organisation file implies; samples travel by daily shuttle, and the travel step and road-closure branch reflect this.

The laboratory also assays the neighbouring Island Gold mine's production samples under contract (island2020). That outside work is not in the organisation file and is left out of the volume here, but it competes for the same furnaces and technicians.
One case is one furnace batch of 28 positions. Preparation is done per sample but recorded here as minutes for the batch's 25 samples.
The assay-lab resource is used for furnace time only; the preparation line is listed separately because it, not the furnace, is usually the constraint.

Staffing check: simulated hands-on time of about 6.5 hours per batch at 300 batches a month implies about 15.6 FTE across all roles, of which about 11 are assay technicians; stated FTE is about 8.2 because the organisation file has only six technicians and one supervisor. The evidence (shift supervisors, an Assay Lab Superintendent, a second mine's samples) points to a larger lab.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.30 for staff, 1.35 for hourly site roles); the added driver role uses the same 1.35 loading.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
